text:
Night execution follow-up — READ ONLY, no build/tests/numerical workload
2026-10-30; scope: R-06/18/21/25/26/28. Requirements reread. Root requested next-mechanism analysis after locality rejection.

1. Decision: reject output-home prototype, retain its historical commit only

Candidate 1343226c96315712d78cfcf4a8804e5885059214 changes only placement, +4*N runtime bytes and unchanged141B Metadata. Root screening data: /home/wishapig/hackathon-overnight/locality-candidate/artifacts/screening/locality-{0..3}-{0,1}.json. All recorded cases remained parallel and correctness passed, so this is not a resource exclusion story. Four complete off samples278.045/272.877/286.131/275.635ms, on264.498/278.027/284.529/282.270ms; medians276.840/280.148ms. One good on sample does not establish benefit.

What is measured:
- Total steals off5910/6844/6096/6075 versus on24083/21195/21726/25960: median grows about3.76x.
- n1536,b128 execute median30.311->31.382ms; b25671.954->75.748ms.
- Fine n128,b8 median steals42->724 and execute0.390->0.499ms; n768,b24 steals821.5->4567.5 and execute4.473->5.687ms. Some other cases improve, insufficient complete gain.
- Diagnosis already measured output migration, but did NOT measure migration under the on candidate. We cannot claim the home hint reduced actual cache misses or dirty-line migrations.

Mechanism explaining rejection (inference tied to code):
- runtime.cpp placement() routes the final decrement to a hash-selected queue, whereas baseline keeps a ready successor in the completing worker's private continuation. Hash-home is usually remote, so it converts a queue-free continuation into enqueue+steal and gives up producer/input cache locality.
- Initial roots and sparse frontiers can be mapped onto occupied workers. Unrestricted thieves preserve utilization but quickly defeat intended ownership; total steals confirm considerably more cross-worker queue consumption, not actual output cache reuse.
- A largest-write-only home ignores the two active read operands, time between updates, cache working-set size and current ownership. Stable hash identity by itself is not a placement policy with a proven reuse opportunity.
- The heavy q6 diagnostic had69.8–76.4ms kernel-weighted CP and only0.42–0.56ms uncovered dispatch latency, including0.31–0.35ms initial wake. Replacing queue management cannot recover tens of milliseconds. q12's3.5–5.5ms gating waits mostly happened with23/24 active kernels, so it is a choice-of-work question already explored via priorities, not missing wakeups.
No recommendation to add sticky ownership, a new priority variant or fixed thread caps. They would introduce another heuristic before proving actual kernel context improvement.

2. Best next candidate: reuse A/L capacity across shape changes, reclaim under pressure

Observed new evidence, independent of locality:
- Baseline screening compute-prepare-execute totals52.177/44.924/46.234/44.252ms per batch. These are allocation/initialization/resource-probe/input-finite-scan/destruction and related surrounding costs, not all removable.
- main.cpp539-545 frees BOTH vectors whenever a.size()!=elements. n1536 is first seen at case12; case16 shrinks to256, discards all large touched pages; case19 grows back1536 and repeats expensive allocation/touch. No case-specific logic is needed to remove this lifecycle behavior.
- In screening case19 the surrounding cost is approximately11–16ms, while case12 initially requires first allocation. Retaining capacity can target repeated allocation/page fault work at the later growth, but cannot eliminate initial allocation, logical resize initialization, input finite checks, real copy, or complete final free. Do not promise the whole45ms.
- This is distinct from failed L-no-init and THP: preserve ordinary vector logical semantics and initially touched storage, without page advice or uninitialized storage. Initial first touch remains timed.

Minimal production changes all in main.cpp:
A. At case header, retain the pair when elements<=a.capacity() AND elements<=l.capacity(). Logical sizes must still become exactly elements: a.resize(elements); l.resize(elements). Shrink keeps touched capacity; later growth within capacity uses already resident pages but still value-initializes newly exposed double elements. Do not leave size at previous max, since __copy currently uses a.begin/end and finite checks/output depend on logical extent.
B. When either capacity is insufficient, release BOTH old vectors before allocating an exact-size replacement pair. No old+new pair coexistence or geometric vector growth. The next case never needs previous values. Empty fresh vectors resize(elements) as baseline, with actual resulting capacity charged.
C. Preserve no-first-Copy semantics: if the first semantic node is not an unconditional full Copy, fill ALL logical L entries to0 each case, including retained prefix. Reused A is fully overwritten by input read. __copy, __zero_upper, operators and output keep exactly n*n logical extent. No pointer retained across cases.
D. Account(actual A capacity+actual L capacity)*sizeof(double), not logical sizes. Existing matrix_bytes/retained_matrices formulas already account capacities but their failure behavior needs reclamation before rejection. Main case_budget and graph budget must deduct full retained capacity. Fresh headroom probe adds retained managed bytes back exactly as today; do not sum full machine memory or let cached capacity vanish from accounting.
E. Initial budget/no-headroom failure: before reading the current payload, drop surplus pair, re-probe and retry with exact required capacity. If available_memory_budget itself throws because free headroom<1MiB while old pair is reclaimable, reclaim the cache before re-probing; otherwise a cache can create a false resource_limited case. Releasing retained runtime is permissible at drained boundary if still required.
F. Later prepare pressure: a seemingly affordable retained matrix cache must not make graph/expansion fall back to serial when exact logical buffers would fit. If preparation ResourceLimit/bad_alloc unwinds before numerical_started and current capacities have surplus, reclaim unused matrix capacity and retry preparation once BEFORE normal resource fallback. No retry after copy or numerical work has begun. A safe non-I/O reclaim sequence after input was read:
   1) release unused L (no numerical call started);
   2) allocate exact-size A, copy its n*n already-read values, then release old A;
   3) allocate exact logical L initialized as required;
   4) re-probe budgets and rerun prepare from clean locals.
   Reclaim peak A_old+A_new does not exceed previous A_old+L_old because L_old capacity>=elements; after old A free, the new pair fits the old pair's footprint. All copying/allocation/retry work timed. Unexpected errors are not classified as memory; a failed exact-fit retry retains the existing resource-limited behavior/reason. Do not simply discard small-case coverage as memory-limited because an optional cache used it.

Implementation tradeoff: D/E/F are the main correctness work, not resize itself. F needs clean per-case preparation scoping, e.g. a local retry loop whose failed Graph/tasks have already unwound; avoid retaining partial graph across reclaim. If root prefers smaller first prototype, use mandatory exact-fit reclaim whenever retained spare would reduce pre-reserved execution headroom and still keep the final one-retry fallback so arbitrary graph sizes aren't disadvantaged. Do not introduce fixed host MB or case IDs.

Acceptance / temporary checks only (parent owns benchmark):
- n,b sequences grow->shrink->grow, repeated same size, non-power-of-two and different b; file headers/count/order preserved. Complete result correctness with original public verifier plus R15.
- First semantic action with Copy and without Copy; custom supported source that leaves some L entries unwritten must retain zero-initialized output, never old-case values. Generic functional R27 gate includes n3/7/16/31.
- Tiny explicit memory where large retained capacity must be released for later smaller but graph-heavy case; resource outcome should match same case with empty buffers if exact mandatory state fits. Include available_memory_budget rejecting before reclaim, and preparation failure before numeric hook.
- Allocation peaks charged, actual capacity included, no repeated numeric operations on retry, input only read once unless explicitly within exempt I/O and correct file position (prefer above A copy).
- Scored complete benchmark only, no excluding first-touch/free from timing. Compare complete-time samples and report case19 as mechanism diagnostic, not a separate score. Metadata stays141B.

3. Other execution mechanisms: limited value or insufficient evidence now

(a) General same-case graph generation/execution overlap is semantically possible but NOT a small replacement. Dependency state records prior writer/readers; each new task can be registered after all accesses resolved, while future writers must depend on earlier readers/writers. Yet a predecessor can complete before a later successor exists, requiring synchronized completion/subscription; CSR arrays and ready arrays currently fixed. Resource fallback must remain possible before numeric begins: once first tasks execute, later graph allocation failure cannot replay serial. A full prepass/reservation or proven bounded dependency window is needed. Total prepare only~20ms/batch and arena is already addressing much of it. No evidence now justifies this concurrency/rollback risk over buffer reuse.

(b) Explicit contraction of chains with outdegree=1 and successor indegree=1 can preserve dependence semantics, but baseline already directly continues one successor without queue. It would save only per-task completion accounting/dependency atomics, a category already tried, plus add preprocessing/group storage. Heavy kernels dominate. No new measurable case supports it.

(c) Overlap Copy with graph preparation would avoid waiting on graph before Copy, but violates the current no-numerical-before-fallback boundary unless preparation is guaranteed first. Copy consumes bandwidth/caches; needs another participant/startup cost; current copy share unmeasured. Existing extracted Copy/postzero costs are small compared with matrix reallocation. Defer.

(d) Idle workers consume~60ms aggregate CPU in heavy q6, but that is NOT60ms elapsed. Event-driven parking could reduce useless polls; old threshold/idle experiments already failed and kernel CP leaves <0.6ms dispatch margin. A materially different exact wait protocol would need fresh evidence of kernel CPU interference, no claim from aggregate idle CPU alone.

Recommendation: retain baseline scheduler and finish arena evaluation. Prototype adaptive A/L capacity reuse next, with cache reclamation preserving R25/R26. If complete benchmark still does not improve reliably, do not force another scheduler redesign just to show activity.
